match.reason: The bank points cover recombinant DNA and replication, but neither teaches the three enzyme roles together (endonucleases cut, ligases join, polymerases build) at the depth this Unit 3/4 point needs, and the recombinant DNA card is broader than the point.

draft.title: Enzymes that manipulate DNA
card: Endonuclease
cuts DNA by breaking the bonds in the sugar-phosphate backbone. A restriction endonuclease cuts at a specific base sequence.
Ligase
joins DNA pieces together by forming bonds in the sugar-phosphate backbone. It seals the gap between two fragments.
Polymerase
builds a new DNA strand by adding nucleotides, using an existing strand as a template.
Cutting, joining and building are three different jobs. Together these enzymes let scientists cut out a piece of DNA, join it to other DNA and make copies.
draft.remember: Endonucleases cut, ligases join and polymerases build.

a.q: Two DNA fragments have been cut from different sources. Which enzyme is used to join them into one molecule?
opts: DNA ligase
DNA polymerase
A restriction endonuclease
A DNA template
a.why: Ligase forms bonds in the sugar-phosphate backbone, which seals fragments together. Polymerase is tempting, but it adds new nucleotides to build a strand rather than joining two existing pieces.
a.clue: Which enzyme seals gaps in the backbone?

b.q: A technician in Geelong mixes a DNA sample with an enzyme. Gel results show the DNA is now in several shorter pieces. What did the enzyme do?
opts: It cut the DNA at specific sequences
It joined the DNA into longer pieces
It built new strands from free nucleotides
It copied the DNA using a template
b.why: Shorter pieces mean the DNA was cut, which is the job of an endonuclease. Building new strands would add nucleotides and make copies, not shorten the DNA.
b.clue: Shorter pieces mean the backbone was broken.

b.best: It cut the DNA at specific sequences

problems.detail: The stem says only 'an enzyme' and that the DNA is in shorter pieces, which shows it was cut but not that the cuts were at specific sequences. The card says only restriction endonucleases cut at a specific sequence. The right option adds a claim the evidence does not support; 'It cut the DNA' or 'It broke the sugar-phosphate backbone' would match the evidence.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both questions have one clear answer. In question b, the right option claims cuts 'at specific sequences', which the stem's evidence of shorter pieces does not show.

b.q: A technician in Geelong mixes a long DNA sample with an enzyme. Tests show the DNA is now in several shorter pieces. What did the enzyme do?
opts: It cut the DNA by breaking backbone bonds
It joined the DNA by forming backbone bonds
It built new strands from free nucleotides
It added nucleotides using a template strand
b.why: One long molecule became several shorter ones, so bonds in the backbone were broken. That is the job of an endonuclease. Forming backbone bonds is tempting because it also involves the backbone, but that is ligase, which would join pieces into longer DNA.
b.clue: Did the DNA get longer or shorter?
